1	# SelectCustomer.php: customer search, selection and customer menu (webERP)
2	
3	Part of [webERP: sales, purchasing, stock, manufacturing, master data, reporting, API…](weberp-sales-purchasing-stock-manufacturing-master-data-repo-151/brief.md) (path from the export's root): its brief says how work moves through the area and what repairs a failed step.
4	
5	## Purpose
6	`webERP/SelectCustomer.php` is the webERP Accounts Receivable page for finding a customer in `debtorsmaster`. It does three things:
7	- Searches by keyword, code, phone, address, type or area. Results are paginated and can be exported to CSV.
8	- Stores the chosen customer in `$_SESSION['CustomerID']` and `$_SESSION['BranchCode']`.
9	- Once a customer is chosen, shows that customer's details, contacts, notes, type notes and an optional geocode map, plus a menu of links to other customer pages.
10	
11	It takes work from other pages' links and from the search form. It hands the selected customer to those other pages through the session and through query-string links.
12	
13	## Contract
14	**In, GET:**
15	- `Select`: sets `$_SESSION['CustomerID']`.
16	- `Area`: pre-fills `$_POST['Area']` and triggers a search.
17	- Other pages also send `DebtorNo` and `DebtorType`, but nothing in the condensed code reads them.
18	
19	**In, POST:**
20	- Search fields: `Keywords`, `CustCode`, `CustPhone`, `CustAdd`, `CustType`, `Area`, plus `FormID`.
21	- Actions: `Search`, `CSV`, `Go`, `Go1`, `Go2`, `Next`, `Previous`, `JustSelectedACustomer`, `SubmitCustomerSelection`.
22	- Paging: `PageOffset`, `PageOffset1`, `PageOffset2`.
23	
24	**In, session:** `CustomerID`, `CustomerType`, `BranchCode`, `SalesmanLogin`, `DisplayRecordsMax`, `reports_dir`, `Theme`, `geocode_integration`, `Extended_CustomerInfo`, `FormID`.
25	
26	**Input handling:** search values are trimmed, uppercased with `mb_strtoupper`, and spaces become `%`.
27	
28	**Out, session:** `$_SESSION['CustomerID']`, `$_SESSION['BranchCode']`.
29	
30	**Out, file:** `$_SESSION['reports_dir'] . '/Customer_Listing_' . date('Y-m-d') . '.csv'`. Each line is `debtorno,name,address1,address2,address3,address4,contactname,typename,phoneno,faxno,email`, with commas escaped in field values.
31	
32	**Out, DB writes:** `UPDATE custbranch SET lat='%s', lng='%s' WHERE branchcode='%s' AND debtorno='%s' LIMIT 1`. This happens only after a successful geocode.
33	
34	**Out, external:** `GET https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search?format=json&q=<encoded address>&limit=1`, with header `User-Agent: webERP-geocoding`. It reads `$json[0]['lat']` and `$json[0]['lon']`. The Leaflet CSS and JS are loaded from unpkg.com.
35	
36	**Reads:**
37	- `debtorsmaster`, `custbranch`, `debtortype`, `areas`, `debtortrans`, `currencies`.
38	- `custcontacts`, `custnotes`, `debtortypenotes`.
39	- `geocode_param` (`map_height`, `map_width`).
40	
41	**Links out, when a customer is selected:**
42	- `CustomerInquiry.php?CustomerID=`
43	- `CustomerAccount.php?CustomerID=`
44	- `Customers.php?DebtorNo=&Modify=No`
45	- `PrintCustStatements.php?FromCust=&ToCust=&EmailOrPrint=print&PrintPDF=Yes`
46	- `PrintCustStatements.php?FromCust=&ToCust=&EmailOrPrint=email&PrintPDF=Yes`. This one needs a customer contact with the statement (email) flag.
47	- `SelectCompletedOrder.php?SelectedCustomer=`
48	- `CustomerPurchases.php?DebtorNo=`
49	- `SelectSalesOrder.php?SelectedCustomer=`
50	- `CustomerAllocations.php?DebtorNo=`
51	- `JobCards.php?DebtorNo=&BranchNo=`
52	- `CustomerReceipt.php?CustomerID=&NewReceipt=Yes&Type=Customer`
53	- `CounterSales.php?DebtorNo=&BranchNo=`. This one appears only when both `CustomerID` and `BranchCode` are set.
54	- `Customers.php`
55	- `CustomerBranches.php?DebtorNo=`
56	- `SelectProduct.php`
57	- `CustEDISetup.php`
58	- `CustLoginSetup.php`
59	- `AddCustomerContacts.php?DebtorNo=`
60	- `AddCustomerNotes.php?DebtorNo=`
61	- `AddCustomerTypeNotes.php?Id=&DebtorType=` (edit)
62	- `AddCustomerTypeNotes.php?Id=&DebtorType=&delete=1` (delete)
63	- `AddCustomerTypeNotes.php?DebtorType=` (add)
64	- `GeocodeSetup.php`
65	
66	The page also calls `wikiLink('Customer', CustomerID)`.
67	
68	## Entry points
69	The single page runs these steps in order:
70	1. `if isset($_GET['Select'])` -> `$_SESSION['CustomerID'] = $_GET['Select']`.
71	2. `if !isset($_SESSION['CustomerID'])` -> set it to `''`.
72	3. `if isset($_GET['Area'])` -> fill `$_POST` with `Area` and trigger a search.
73	4. `if !isset($_SESSION['CustomerType'])` -> set it to `''`.
74	5. `if isset($_POST['JustSelectedACustomer'])`:
75	   - `if isset($_POST['SubmitCustomerSelection'])` -> loop the array and set `$_SESSION['CustomerID']` and `$_SESSION['BranchCode']`.
76	   - `elseif !isset($_POST['Search'])` -> error "Unable to identify the selected customer".
77	6. `if isset($_POST['Go1']) or isset($_POST['Go2'])` -> `$_POST['PageOffset']` is taken from that button's value.
78	7. `if !isset($_POST['PageOffset'])` -> 1. `else if $_POST['PageOffset'] == 0` -> 1.
79	8. `if isset($_POST['Search']) or isset($_POST['CSV']) or isset($_POST['Go']) or isset($_POST['Next']) or isset($_POST['Previous'])` -> unset `$_POST['JustSelectedACustomer']`, then build and run the SQL.
80	9. Display switch:
81	   - `if $_SESSION['CustomerID'] != '' AND !isset($_POST['Search']) AND !isset($_POST['CSV'])` -> show the customer details and menu.
82	   - `else` -> show the search form.
83	
84	No permission check is shown anywhere on the page.
85	
86	## Decisions
87	**Search query**
88	- Keywords, CustCode and CustPhone use `LIKE` with `%`.
89	- CustPhone adds `OR custbranch.phoneno IS NULL`, so branches with no phone number match any phone search.
90	- CustAdd matches `address1`, `address2`, `address3` and `address4` with `OR`.
91	- When no criterion is set (empty or `'ALL'`), no `WHERE` is added and all debtors are included.
92	- `if strlen($_POST['CustType']) > 0 and != 'ALL'` -> `AND debtortype.typename = CustType`.
93	- `if strlen($_POST['Area']) > 0 and != 'ALL'` -> `AND custbranch.area = Area`.
94	- `if $_SESSION['SalesmanLogin'] != ''` -> `AND custbranch.salesman = SalesmanLogin`.
95	- `if DB_num_rows == 1` -> set `CustomerID` and `BranchCode` from the row and unset `$_POST['Search']`. The page then goes straight to the customer view.
96	- `if DB_num_rows == 0` -> info message "No customer records contain the selected text - please alter your search criteria and try again".
97	
98	**Search form**
99	- `if isset($_POST['CustType'])` -> read `debtortype`. `if DB_num_rows == 0` -> `$DataError = 1`, error with a link to Setup Types, and the select box is skipped.
100	- Else a select box is built with `ALL` shown as "Any", and the option whose `typename == $_POST['CustType']` is marked selected.
101	- Areas are read the same way. `if DB_num_rows == 0` -> `$DataError = 1`, error with a link to Setup Areas, and the select is skipped.
102	- Else a select named `Area` is built, and the option whose `areacode == $_POST['Area']` is selected.
103	- `if isset($_SESSION['SalesmanLogin']) and != ''` -> warning message.
104	- `if isset($SearchResult)` -> unset `CustomerID`, `$ListCount = DB_num_rows`, `$ListPageMax = ceil($ListCount / DisplayRecordsMax)`.
105	
106	**Pagination and CSV**
107	- `if !isset($_POST['CSV'])`: `Next` with `PageOffset < ListPageMax` -> +1, and `Previous` with `PageOffset > 1` -> -1.
108	- `if $ListPageMax > 1` -> page selector and Previous/Next buttons at the top and bottom.
109	- `if isset($_POST['CSV'])` -> write all results to the CSV file.
110	- Otherwise `DB_data_seek` to `(PageOffset - 1) * DisplayRecordsMax` and render rows. The loop stops when `RowIndex == DisplayRecordsMax`.
111	- Row fields: `debtorno`, `branchcode`, `name`, `brname` (null shown as `''`), `contactname`, `typename`, `phoneno`, `faxno`, and `email` as a `mailto` link.
112	
113	**Customer view**
114	- If the first lookup returns nothing: read `CustomerName`, `PhoneNo` and `BranchName` from `debtorsmaster` joined to `custbranch`. `if isset($_SESSION['BranchCode'])` -> `AND custbranch.branchcode = BranchCode`.
115	- `$Msg` is echoed if `mb_strlen > 1`.
116	- `if $_SESSION['CustomerID'] != ''` -> show type, last paid, customer since and total spend.
117	- `lastpaiddate == 0` -> "No receipts from this customer." Otherwise show date, amount and days since.
118	- `total == 0` -> "No Spend from this Customer." Otherwise show Total Spend.
119	- Contacts: rows present -> table with Edit, Delete and Add New Contact links. No rows and `CustomerID != ''` -> only the Add New Contact link.
120	- `if BranchCode set and != ''` -> a branch contact row (`branchcode`, `contactname`, `phoneno`, `email` from `custbranch`) is appended.
121	- Notes: rows present -> table of all notes. No rows and `CustomerID != ''` -> only the "Add New Note for this Customer" link.
122	- Type notes (`debtortypenotes`) run only `if $_SESSION['Extended_CustomerInfo'] == 1`. Rows present -> table with edit, delete and add links. No rows and `CustomerID != ''` -> add link only. No rows and no customer -> nothing.
123	
124	**Geocode map** (`if $_SESSION['geocode_integration'] == 1`; otherwise the block is skipped)
125	- `if DB_num_rows($Result) == 0` for `geocode_param` -> message "You must first setup the geocode parameters" with a link to `GeocodeSetup.php`, then the footer, then exit.
126	- `if $Lat == 0 and braddress1 != '' and BranchCode != ''` -> call Nominatim.
127	- `if $buffer === false` -> `$geocode_pending = false`, message "Unable to update GeoCode for CustomerID: [id] - Connection failed".
128	- If the JSON is empty or `$json[0]['lat']` or `['lon']` is missing -> `$geocode_pending = false`, message "... - No results found".
129	- On success -> `UPDATE custbranch`.
130	- `if $Lat == 0` -> "Mapping is enabled, but no Mapping data to display for this Customer."
131	- `if $Lat != 0` -> a Leaflet map at `[$Lat, $Lng]`, zoom 14, with an OpenStreetMap tile layer and a marker popup showing the branch name and addresses.
132	
133	## Order and failure
134	- The `$_GET['Select']` and `$_POST['SubmitCustomerSelection']` selections are written to the session before any query runs, so the selection stays even if a later query fails.
135	- No handler is shown around any `DB_query`. Each call passes only an error-message parameter, for example "The searched customer records requested cannot be retrieved because". Whether it halts is not shown.
136	- The geocode loop `while $geocode_pending` runs once, with `usleep(1000000)` before the request. It ends when `$geocode_pending` is set false.
137	- The `custbranch` UPDATE has no failure handling. A failed Nominatim call leaves `lat` at 0, so the next page view tries again.
138	- The CSV `fopen` and `fwrite` results are not checked.
139	
140	## Connections
141	- **`webERP/CustomerAccount.php`**
142	  - Reads `$_GET['CustomerID']`, or else `$_SESSION['CustomerID']`.
143	  - If neither is set, it prints a message and a link back to `SelectCustomer.php`.
144	  - If `$_SESSION['SalesmanLogin'] != ''`, it checks `custbranch.salesman`. If there is no row: 'There is no salesman data set for this customer'. If the salesman does not match: 'You have no authority to review this customer account'. Both exit.
145	  - It filters `debtortrans.salesperson = SalesmanLogin`.
146	  - It shows settled transactions only if `Show_Settled_LastMonth == 1`.
147	  - It labels transaction types 10 (invoice), 11 (credit) and 12 (receipt).
148	  - Receipt rendering: for 12, `totalamount < 0` renders as a credit with an allocation link, and `> 0` renders as a charge with no links.
149	- **`webERP/CustLoginSetup.php`**
150	  - If `!isset($_SESSION['CustomerID'])` -> info message with a redirect link to `SelectCustomer.php`, then exit. It uses the `CustomerID` this page stores in the session.

- `if isset($_POST['CustType'])` -> read `debtortype`. `if DB_num_rows == 0` -> `$DataError = 1`, error with a link to Setup Types, and the select box is skipped.

- Areas are read the same way. `if DB_num_rows == 0` -> `$DataError = 1`, error with a link to Setup Areas, and the select is skipped.
- Else a select named `Area` is built, and the option whose `areacode == $_POST['Area']` is selected.
- `if isset($_SESSION['SalesmanLogin']) and != ''` -> warning message.
- `if isset($SearchResult)` -> unset `CustomerID`, `$ListCount = DB_num_rows`, `$ListPageMax = ceil($ListCount / DisplayRecordsMax)`.

**Pagination and CSV**
- `if !isset($_POST['CSV'])`: `Next` with `PageOffset < ListPageMax` -> +1, and `Previous` with `PageOffset > 1` -> -1.
- `if $ListPageMax > 1` -> page selector and Previous/Next buttons at the top and bottom.
- `if isset($_POST['CSV'])` -> write all results to the CSV file.
- Otherwise `DB_data_seek` to `(PageOffset - 1) * DisplayRecordsMax` and render rows. The loop stops when `RowIndex == DisplayRecordsMax`.
- Row fields: `debtorno`, `branchcode`, `name`, `brname` (null shown as `''`), `contactname`, `typename`, `phoneno`, `faxno`, and `email` as a `mailto` link.

**Customer view**
- If the first lookup returns nothing: read `CustomerName`, `PhoneNo` and `BranchName` from `debtorsmaster` joined to `custbranch`. `if isset($_SESSION['BranchCode'])` -> `AND custbranch.branchcode = BranchCode`.
- `$Msg` is echoed if `mb_strlen > 1`.
- `if $_SESSION['CustomerID'] != ''` -> show type, last paid, customer since and total spend.
- `lastpaiddate == 0` -> "No receipts from this customer." Otherwise show date, amount and days since.
- `total == 0` -> "No Spend from this Customer." Otherwise show Total Spend.
- Contacts: rows present -> table with Edit, Delete and Add New Contact links. No rows and `CustomerID != ''` -> only the Add New Contact link.
- `if BranchCode set and != ''` -> a branch contact row (`branchcode`, `contactname`, `phoneno`, `email` from `custbranch`) is appended.
- Notes: rows present -> table of all notes. No rows and `CustomerID != ''` -> only the "Add New Note for this Customer" link.
- Type notes (`debtortypenotes`) run only `if $_SESSION['Extended_CustomerInfo'] == 1`. Rows present -> table with edit, delete and add links. No rows and `CustomerID != ''` -> add link only. No rows and no customer -> nothing.

**Geocode map** (`if $_SESSION['geocode_integration'] == 1`; otherwise the block is skipped)
- `if DB_num_rows($Result) == 0` for `geocode_param` -> message "You must first setup the geocode parameters" with a link to `GeocodeSetup.php`, then the footer, then exit.
- `if $Lat == 0 and braddress1 != '' and BranchCode != ''` -> call Nominatim.
- `if $buffer === false` -> `$geocode_pending = false`, message "Unable to update GeoCode for CustomerID: [id] - Connection failed".
- If the JSON is empty or `$json[0]['lat']` or `['lon']` is missing -> `$geocode_pending = false`, message "... - No results found".
- On success -> `UPDATE custbranch`.
- `if $Lat == 0` -> "Mapping is enabled, but no Mapping data to display for this Customer."
- `if $Lat != 0` -> a Leaflet map at `[$Lat, $Lng]`, zoom 14, with an OpenStreetMap tile layer and a marker popup showing the branch name and addresses.

## Order and failure
- The `$_GET['Select']` and `$_POST['SubmitCustomerSelection']` selections are written to the session before any query runs, so the selection stays even if a later query fails.
- No handler is shown around any `DB_query`. Each call passes only an error-message parameter, for example "The searched customer records requested cannot be retrieved because". Whether it halts is not shown.
- The geocode loop `while $geocode_pending` runs once, with `usleep(1000000)` before the request. It ends when `$geocode_pending` is set false.
- The `custbranch` UPDATE has no failure handling. A failed Nominatim call leaves `lat` at 0, so the next page view tries again.
- The CSV `fopen` and `fwrite` results are not checked.

## Connections
- **`webERP/CustomerAccount.php`**
  - Reads `$_GET['CustomerID']`, or else `$_SESSION['CustomerID']`.
  - If neither is set, it prints a message and a link back to `SelectCustomer.php`.
  - If `$_SESSION['SalesmanLogin'] != ''`, it checks `custbranch.salesman`. If there is no row: 'There is no salesman data set for this customer'. If the salesman does not match: 'You have no authority to review this customer account'. Both exit.
  - It filters `debtortrans.salesperson = SalesmanLogin`.
  - It shows settled transactions only if `Show_Settled_LastMonth == 1`.
  - It labels transaction types 10 (invoice), 11 (credit) and 12 (receipt).
  - Receipt rendering: for 12, `totalamount < 0` renders as a credit with an allocation link, and `> 0` renders as a charge with no links.
- **`webERP/CustLoginSetup.php`**
  - If `!isset($_SESSION['CustomerID'])` -> info message with a redirect link to `SelectCustomer.php`, then exit. It uses the `CustomerID` this page stores in the session.

They read the `debtortrans`, `debtorsmaster`, `paymentterms`, `holdreasons`, `systypes`, `salesman`, `suppliers`, `supptrans` and `currencies` tables. MRP.php is only a truncated fragment.
6	
7	## Contract
8	**Inputs (POST/session; the page is reached by a form POST).**
9	
10	AgedDebtors:
11	- `FromCriteria` and `ToCriteria` are debtor-number strings. The form has maxlength 6 and defaults '0' and 'zzzzzz'.
12	- `All_Or_Overdues` is `All`, `OverduesOnly` or `HeldOnly`.
13	- `Salesman` is optional. `Currency` is a currabrev code.
14	- `DetailedReport` is `Yes` or `No`.
15	- `PrintPDF` or `View` submits the form.
16	- Session: `SalesmanLogin`, `UsersRealName`, `PastDueDays1`, `PastDueDays2`, `CompanyRecord['currencydefault']`, `CompanyRecord['coyname']`, `PageSize`, `DatabaseName`, `DefaultDateFormat`.
17	
18	AgedSuppliers:
19	- `FromCriteria` and `ToCriteria` have maxlength 6 and default "1" and "zzzzzz".
20	- `All_Or_Overdues` is `All` or `OverduesOnly`. `Currency` is a currabrev code. `DetailedReport` is `Yes` or `No`.
21	- `PrintPDF` or `View` submits the form.
22	- Session: `PastDueDays1`, `PastDueDays2`, `PageSize`, `DatabaseName`, `CompanyRecord`, `DefaultDateFormat`.
23	
24	MRP: `$_POST['submit']`.
25	
26	**Outputs.**
27	- The reports go to the browser as HTML, wrapped in includes/header.php and includes/footer.php. If `PrintPDF` is set, they go as a PDF (Dompdf) instead.
28	- The PDF is landscape at `$_SESSION['PageSize']`. It is streamed with `Attachment=>false` and named `<DatabaseName>_AgedDebtors_Y-m-d.pdf` or `<DatabaseName>_AgedCreditors_<date>.pdf`.
29	- The HTML links `css/reports.css` when `PrintPDF` is set.
30	- Debtor summary columns: balance, current, due, overdue1, overdue2.
31	- Supplier summary columns: Supplier, Balance, Current, Due Now, `[PastDueDays1] Days Over`, `[PastDueDays2] Days Over`.
32	- Both reports end with a total row (`TotBal`, `TotCurr`, `TotDue`, `TotOD1`, `TotOD2`).
33	
34	## Entry points
35	**AgedDebtors.php**
36	- Form display: `if (!isset(FromCriteria) or !isset(ToCriteria))` -> show the form. Otherwise the form is skipped.
37	- Report: `if (PrintPDF or View) and isset(FromCriteria) and mb_strlen(FromCriteria)>=1 and isset(ToCriteria) and mb_strlen(ToCriteria)>=1` -> generate. No permission check, no format check and no existence check on the criteria, `Currency` or `Salesman`.
38	
39	**AgedSuppliers.php**
40	- Form: same `!isset(FromCriteria) or !isset(ToCriteria)` test.
41	- Report: same guard as AgedDebtors (`PrintPDF or View`, plus both criteria set with length >= 1). Nothing else is checked. There is no `FromCriteria <= ToCriteria` check, and no check that `PastDueDays1` and `PastDueDays2` are set.
42	
43	**MRP.php**
44	- `if isset($_POST['submit'])` -> continues beyond the fragment, so its behaviour is not known.
45	
46	## Decisions
47	**AgedDebtors**
48	- `$_SESSION['SalesmanLogin'] != ''` -> `$_POST['Salesman']` is overridden with the session value. The form shows `UsersRealName` as text instead of the salesman select.
49	- `$_SESSION['SalesmanLogin'] == ''` -> the form shows the salesman select, with an empty value meaning "All Salespeople".
50	- `trim($_POST['Salesman']) != ''` -> a salesman filter is added to the WHERE clause. The salesman name is also looked up with `SELECT salesmanname FROM salesman WHERE salesmancode=...` and shown in the report header.
51	- `All_Or_Overdues=='All'` -> HAVING sum > `CurrencyTolerance($_SESSION['CompanyRecord']['currencydefault'])`.
52	- `All_Or_Overdues=='OverduesOnly'` -> HAVING overdue1 calculation > `CurrencyTolerance(currencydefault)`.
53	- `All_Or_Overdues=='HeldOnly'` -> WHERE `holdreasons.dissallowinvoices=1` and HAVING `ABS(sum)` > `CurrencyTolerance(currencydefault)`.
54	- `paymentterms.daysbeforedue > 0` -> due, overdue1 and overdue2 are counted as days from `trandate`. Otherwise they are counted as days from the end of the month following `trandate`.
55	- `DetailedReport=='Yes'` -> a nested query per customer reads `debtorsmaster`, `paymentterms`, `debtortrans` and `systypes`.
56	  - If `SalesmanLogin != ''` it adds `AND debtortrans.salesperson=SalesmanLogin`.
57	  - On failure the error message is "The details of outstanding transactions for customer [debtorno] could not be retrieved".
58	  - It sets `$FontSize=8`.
59	- `isset(PrintPDF)` -> Dompdf output. Otherwise header, HTML and footer.
60	- Form selection: the currency option that equals `currencydefault` is selected. If `DetailedReport` is unset, "Summary Report" (No) is selected. If it is `Yes`, "Detailed Report" is selected.
61	
62	**AgedSuppliers**
63	- `All_Or_Overdues=='All'` -> HAVING `ROUND(ABS(SUM(supptrans.balance)), currencies.decimalplaces) > CurrencyTolerance($_POST['Currency'])`.
64	- `All_Or_Overdues` is anything else (so `OverduesOnly`) -> HAVING `SUM(IF(...)) > 0`, over the overdue buckets.
65	- WHERE: `suppliers.supplierid >= From`, `suppliers.supplierid <= To` and `suppliers.currcode = Currency`, all as concatenated strings.
66	- `paymentterms.daysbeforedue > 0`:
67	  - Age is `TO_DAYS(Now()) - TO_DAYS(trandate)`, compared to `daysbeforedue`.
68	  - overdue1 sums the balance when age > `daysbeforedue` and age >= `daysbeforedue + PastDueDays1`. overdue2 is the same with `PastDueDays2`.
69	- Otherwise the age is `TO_DAYS(Now()) - TO_DAYS(ADDDATE(last_day(trandate), dayinfollowingmonth))`. The balance is summed into overdue1 when this is >= `PastDueDays1`, and into overdue2 when it is >= `PastDueDays2`.
70	- `DetailedReport=='Yes'` -> a per-supplier detail query joins `suppliers`, `paymentterms`, `supptrans` and `systypes`. It filters `ABS(balance) > CurrencyTolerance($_POST['Currency'])`, `settled=0` and `supplierno`.
71	- `isset(PrintPDF)` -> Dompdf. Otherwise HTML with a close button.
72	
73	## Order and failure
74	- Totals accumulate during the `while DB_fetch_array(...)` loop over customers or suppliers. The detail loop is nested inside it. The total row is written after the loop.
75	- AgedSuppliers runs `DB_query($SQL,'','',false,false)`. The fourth argument false means errors are not trapped, and nothing renders an error message.
76	- AgedDebtors has no handler around the nested detail query, so an error goes to the caller. The `salesman` and `currencies` form queries also have no error handling.
77	- Nothing is saved or committed by these pages. They only read.
78	- Nothing handles Dompdf failures.
79	
80	## Connections
81	- Tables read:
82	  - `debtortrans`: `balance` is a stored generated column, `(ovamount+ovgst+ovfreight+ovdiscount)-alloc`. `salesperson varchar(4)` is indexed. `settled` is 0 or 1.
83	  - `supptrans`: the base schema has no `balance` column. `webERP/sql/updates/33.php` adds a calculated `balance` column to it. The AgedSuppliers report depends on that update.
84	  - `holdreasons`: `dissallowinvoices tinyint NOT NULL DEFAULT '-1'`. HeldOnly matches only the value 1.
85	  - Also read: `debtorsmaster`, `paymentterms`, `systypes`, `salesman` (salesmancode, salesmanname), `currencies` (currency, currabrev) and `suppliers`.
86	- Functions called, whose behaviour is not in this topic: `CurrencyTolerance()`, `DB_query()`, `DB_fetch_array()`, `DB_num_rows()`.
87	- Report library: Dompdf.
88	- Includes: session, header and footer.
89	- A `taxprovinces` query (`SELECT taxprovinceid, taxprovincename FROM taxprovinces`) was noted for AgedSuppliers, but its place in the page is unclear.
90	- Nothing else sends to these pages. Only a user's browser POST reaches them.
91	
92	## Conclusions
93	- HeldOnly lists only customers whose hold reason has `dissallowinvoices=1`. Reasons with the default -1 or 0 are excluded.
94	- OverduesOnly in AgedDebtors and AgedSuppliers drops customers and suppliers with no overdue amount.
95	- AgedDebtors compares against the tolerance for the company default currency, even if the user picks another `Currency`. AgedSuppliers uses the selected currency's tolerance.
96	- The "All" modes hide balances at or below the tolerance.
97	- In AgedDebtors, a user with `SalesmanLogin` is restricted to their own salesman. The detail query also filters on `debtortrans.salesperson`, but the summary query only adds the `Salesman` filter.
98	- Default 'zzzzzz' makes the range cover all ordinary codes. A reversed range silently gives an empty report.
99	- Submitting the same form twice gives the same read-only output, so nothing is duplicated.
100	- `$_SESSION['PastDueDays1']` and `PastDueDays2` are used directly. If they are missing, the report fails or errors.
101	- AgedDebtors has no filter on Currency shown in the overview. The form shows the selection, but the query's use of it is not shown here.
102	
103	## Hazards
104	- `FromCriteria`, `ToCriteria`, `Currency` and `Salesman` are concatenated into SQL without escaping, so SQL injection is possible.
105	- Errors are untrapped in AgedSuppliers and are not shown to the user.
106	- There is no permission check on running these reports.
107	- If the `supptrans.balance` upgrade (update 33) is missing, the AgedSuppliers queries fail.

# webERP aged debtors, aged suppliers and MRP report pages (`webERP/AgedDebtors.php`, `webERP/AgedSuppliers.php`, `webERP/MRP.php`)

Part of [webERP report writer, printable reports and report/admin pages: area overview](weberp-report-writer-printable-reports-and-report-admin-page-153/brief.md) (path from the export's root): its brief says how work moves through the area and what repairs a failed step.

Three report pages. AgedDebtors and AgedSuppliers each show a criteria form and build an aged-balance report as HTML or PDF (Dompdf). They read the `debtortrans`, `debtorsmaster`, `paymentterms`, `holdreasons`, `systypes`, `salesman`, `suppliers`, `supptrans` and `currencies` tables. MRP.php is only a truncated fragment.

## Contract
**Inputs (POST/session; the page is reached by a form POST).**

AgedDebtors:
- `FromCriteria` and `ToCriteria` are debtor-number strings. The form has maxlength 6 and defaults '0' and 'zzzzzz'.
- `All_Or_Overdues` is `All`, `OverduesOnly` or `HeldOnly`.
- `Salesman` is optional. `Currency` is a currabrev code.
- `DetailedReport` is `Yes` or `No`.
- `PrintPDF` or `View` submits the form.
- Session: `SalesmanLogin`, `UsersRealName`, `PastDueDays1`, `PastDueDays2`, `CompanyRecord['currencydefault']`, `CompanyRecord['coyname']`, `PageSize`, `DatabaseName`, `DefaultDateFormat`.

AgedSuppliers:
- `FromCriteria` and `ToCriteria` have maxlength 6 and default "1" and "zzzzzz".
- `All_Or_Overdues` is `All` or `OverduesOnly`. `Currency` is a currabrev code. `DetailedReport` is `Yes` or `No`.
- `PrintPDF` or `View` submits the form.
- Session: `PastDueDays1`, `PastDueDays2`, `PageSize`, `DatabaseName`, `CompanyRecord`, `DefaultDateFormat`.

MRP: `$_POST['submit']`.

**Outputs.**
- The reports go to the browser as HTML, wrapped in includes/header.php and includes/footer.php. If `PrintPDF` is set, they go as a PDF (Dompdf) instead.
- The PDF is landscape at `$_SESSION['PageSize']`. It is streamed with `Attachment=>false` and named `<DatabaseName>_AgedDebtors_Y-m-d.pdf` or `<DatabaseName>_AgedCreditors_<date>.pdf`.
- The HTML links `css/reports.css` when `PrintPDF` is set.
- Debtor summary columns: balance, current, due, overdue1, overdue2.
- Supplier summary columns: Supplier, Balance, Current, Due Now, `[PastDueDays1] Days Over`, `[PastDueDays2] Days Over`.
- Both reports end with a total row (`TotBal`, `TotCurr`, `TotDue`, `TotOD1`, `TotOD2`).

## Entry points
**AgedDebtors.php**
- Form display: `if (!isset(FromCriteria) or !isset(ToCriteria))` -> show the form. Otherwise the form is skipped.
- Report: `if (PrintPDF or View) and isset(FromCriteria) and mb_strlen(FromCriteria)>=1 and isset(ToCriteria) and mb_strlen(ToCriteria)>=1` -> generate. No permission check, no format check and no existence check on the criteria, `Currency` or `Salesman`.

**AgedSuppliers.php**
- Form: same `!isset(FromCriteria) or !isset(ToCriteria)` test.
- Report: same guard as AgedDebtors (`PrintPDF or View`, plus both criteria set with length >= 1). Nothing else is checked. There is no `FromCriteria <= ToCriteria` check, and no check that `PastDueDays1` and `PastDueDays2` are set.

**MRP.php**
- `if isset($_POST['submit'])` -> continues beyond the fragment, so its behaviour is not known.

## Decisions
**AgedDebtors**
- `$_SESSION['SalesmanLogin'] != ''` -> `$_POST['Salesman']` is overridden with the session value. The form shows `UsersRealName` as text instead of the salesman select.
- `$_SESSION['SalesmanLogin'] == ''` -> the form shows the salesman select, with an empty value meaning "All Salespeople".
- `trim($_POST['Salesman']) != ''` -> a salesman filter is added to the WHERE clause. The salesman name is also looked up with `SELECT salesmanname FROM salesman WHERE salesmancode=...` and shown in the report header.
- `All_Or_Overdues=='All'` -> HAVING sum > `CurrencyTolerance($_SESSION['CompanyRecord']['currencydefault'])`.
- `All_Or_Overdues=='OverduesOnly'` -> HAVING overdue1 calculation > `CurrencyTolerance(currencydefault)`.
- `All_Or_Overdues=='HeldOnly'` -> WHERE `holdreasons.dissallowinvoices=1` and HAVING `ABS(sum)` > `CurrencyTolerance(currencydefault)`.
- `paymentterms.daysbeforedue > 0` -> due, overdue1 and overdue2 are counted as days from `trandate`. Otherwise they are counted as days from the end of the month following `trandate`.
- `DetailedReport=='Yes'` -> a nested query per customer reads `debtorsmaster`, `paymentterms`, `debtortrans` and `systypes`.
  - If `SalesmanLogin != ''` it adds `AND debtortrans.salesperson=SalesmanLogin`.
  - On failure the error message is "The details of outstanding transactions for customer [debtorno] could not be retrieved".
  - It sets `$FontSize=8`.
- `isset(PrintPDF)` -> Dompdf output. Otherwise header, HTML and footer.
- Form selection: the currency option that equals `currencydefault` is selected. If `DetailedReport` is unset, "Summary Report" (No) is selected. If it is `Yes`, "Detailed Report" is selected.

**AgedSuppliers**
- `All_Or_Overdues=='All'` -> HAVING `ROUND(ABS(SUM(supptrans.balance)), currencies.decimalplaces) > CurrencyTolerance($_POST['Currency'])`.
- `All_Or_Overdues` is anything else (so `OverduesOnly`) -> HAVING `SUM(IF(...)) > 0`, over the overdue buckets.
- WHERE: `suppliers.supplierid >= From`, `suppliers.supplierid <= To` and `suppliers.currcode = Currency`, all as concatenated strings.
- `paymentterms.daysbeforedue > 0`:
  - Age is `TO_DAYS(Now()) - TO_DAYS(trandate)`, compared to `daysbeforedue`.
  - overdue1 sums the balance when age > `daysbeforedue` and age >= `daysbeforedue + PastDueDays1`. overdue2 is the same with `PastDueDays2`.
- Otherwise the age is `TO_DAYS(Now()) - TO_DAYS(ADDDATE(last_day(trandate), dayinfollowingmonth))`. The balance is summed into overdue1 when this is >= `PastDueDays1`, and into overdue2 when it is >= `PastDueDays2`.
- `DetailedReport=='Yes'` -> a per-supplier detail query joins `suppliers`, `paymentterms`, `supptrans` and `systypes`. It filters `ABS(balance) > CurrencyTolerance($_POST['Currency'])`, `settled=0` and `supplierno`.
- `isset(PrintPDF)` -> Dompdf. Otherwise HTML with a close button.

## Order and failure
- Totals accumulate during the `while DB_fetch_array(...)` loop over customers or suppliers. The detail loop is nested inside it. The total row is written after the loop.
- AgedSuppliers runs `DB_query($SQL,'','',false,false)`. The fourth argument false means errors are not trapped, and nothing renders an error message.
- AgedDebtors has no handler around the nested detail query, so an error goes to the caller. The `salesman` and `currencies` form queries also have no error handling.
- Nothing is saved or committed by these pages. They only read.
- Nothing handles Dompdf failures.

## Connections
- Tables read:
  - `debtortrans`: `balance` is a stored generated column, `(ovamount+ovgst+ovfreight+ovdiscount)-alloc`. `salesperson varchar(4)` is indexed. `settled` is 0 or 1.
  - `supptrans`: the base schema has no `balance` column. `webERP/sql/updates/33.php` adds a calculated `balance` column to it. The AgedSuppliers report depends on that update.
  - `holdreasons`: `dissallowinvoices tinyint NOT NULL DEFAULT '-1'`. HeldOnly matches only the value 1.
  - Also read: `debtorsmaster`, `paymentterms`, `systypes`, `salesman` (salesmancode, salesmanname), `currencies` (currency, currabrev) and `suppliers`.
- Functions called, whose behaviour is not in this topic: `CurrencyTolerance()`, `DB_query()`, `DB_fetch_array()`, `DB_num_rows()`.
- Report library: Dompdf.
- Includes: session, header and footer.
- A `taxprovinces` query (`SELECT taxprovinceid, taxprovincename FROM taxprovinces`) was noted for AgedSuppliers, but its place in the page is unclear.
- Nothing else sends to these pages. Only a user's browser POST reaches them.

## Conclusions
- HeldOnly lists only customers whose hold reason has `dissallowinvoices=1`. Reasons with the default -1 or 0 are excluded.
- OverduesOnly in AgedDebtors and AgedSuppliers drops customers and suppliers with no overdue amount.
- AgedDebtors compares against the tolerance for the company default currency, even if the user picks another `Currency`. AgedSuppliers uses the selected currency's tolerance.
- The "All" modes hide balances at or below the tolerance.
- In AgedDebtors, a user with `SalesmanLogin` is restricted to their own salesman. The detail query also filters on `debtortrans.salesperson`, but the summary query only adds the `Salesman` filter.
- Default 'zzzzzz' makes the range cover all ordinary codes. A reversed range silently gives an empty report.
- Submitting the same form twice gives the same read-only output, so nothing is duplicated.
- `$_SESSION['PastDueDays1']` and `PastDueDays2` are used directly. If they are missing, the report fails or errors.
- AgedDebtors has no filter on Currency shown in the overview. The form shows the selection, but the query's use of it is not shown here.

## Hazards
- `FromCriteria`, `ToCriteria`, `Currency` and `Salesman` are concatenated into SQL without escaping, so SQL injection is possible.
- Errors are untrapped in AgedSuppliers and are not shown to the user.
- There is no permission check on running these reports.
- If the `supptrans.balance` upgrade (update 33) is missing, the AgedSuppliers queries fail.
- The MRP.php fragment is truncated, so nothing can be concluded about it.

Customer Statements

187 188

Customer statements can either be printed or emailed directly to all the customers in the selected range, that have a contact defined as receiving a statement. If there are no contacts defined for the customer that have the statement flag set to yes then their statement will not be emailed to them. If the customer has many contacts with several of them having the statement flag set to yes then all those contacts will receive a copy of the pdf statement.

189

If the customer has any contacts that have the statement flag set then it will not be possible to print their statement so as to avoid sending both a printed statement and an email statement

195 196

Customer Notes

197 198

Customer notes containing any text - a web-link if required and a date can be entered from the Select Customer screen - for the selected customer. The notes are displayed in sequence of priority - so pressing issues appear at the top of the list. These notes might contain information about recent contact with the customer or disputes. There is no checking on the content of the notes and no limit to either the number of notes nor the number of characters that can be used.

199 200

Customer Type Notes

201 202

As well as unlimited notes on individual customers, webERP has the functionality to store an unlimited number of notes on groups of customers based on the debtor type field. As with the notes on individual customers , these notes are displayed in order of priority, and can contain a URL as well as the free form note.

203 204 205

Shippers

206 207

This table is only used as a reference to the method of transportation that the invoice delivery was effected by. The shippers name is what is used in the look ups and the code is a system maintained counter which is stored in the database to reference the freight company used. The consignment note reference can be stored against the transaction in the reference field. In this way a full proof of delivery trail can be maintained.

208 209

Shipment cost calculations can be automated and the result automatically added to invoices. The least cost shipper is calculated and modified on the order. This system requires active maintenance of the shipment costs tables for each shipper. The shipper costs table shows the cost per kg and metre cubed for freight to destination cities. A substantial amount of data is required. For the system to calculate freight, it also requires that each part have a defined volume and weight set up from which the total order weight and volume is determined for use in the freight calculations.

210 211

input.new_string:
A customers Credit Status can be altered at any time, but only by users with the credit control security token. Other users see the status and the limit and cannot change them. A change made here is recorded in the credit control history of the customer. A status can have three effects, set in Credit Status Code Maintenance: invoices allowed (normal), on watch, or on stop. See Credit Control.

Note: This will never show on any reports invoices, credits or statement intended for the customers eyes.

Credit Limit

This is a required field which accepts any positive value. It is used to warn about, or hold, orders that take the customer over the limit - see Credit Control. Only credit control can change it, normally by recording a credit review so that the new limit and the reason for it are kept together.

tool_use_result.originalFile:
Accounts Receivable

Overview

A primary function of the system is to track the amounts owed to the business by customers in both local and foreign currency. The system shows, invoice-by-invoice, the balance on the account and does not lose the detail of what makes the account up in a balance brought forward - it is an "open item" system. When payments received from customers are entered and allocated to invoices, the differences on exchange are calculated and posted to the general ledger - that is only if integration to the general ledger is enabled from the company preferences page under the setup tab.

Features

  • Overdues inquiry that takes into account delivery days to the customer's branch and the actual terms applicable to the customer, supported by detailed inquiry of actual invoices overdue.
  • Full on-screen inquiry on a customer's account, complete with invoice details and narrative which appeared on the invoice. Inquiries on payments received will show how a payment was allocated to invoices and the difference on exchange attributable to each invoice.
  • Full integration with stock records and general ledger -a full trail of journals for each transaction is maintained - a drill down to the general ledger transactions for each transaction on a customers account is available from the customer inquiry page.
  • Open item - full analysis of the outstanding balance is maintained and printed on statements for maximum information to the customer.
  • Flexible user definable sales analysis reports to pdf or spreadsheet (csv - comma separated values).
  • Retrospective - de-allocation and re-allocation of receipts or credit notes against charges with re-calculation of differences on exchange and corresponding general ledger journals
  • Any number of branch - delivery addresses can be added serviced by different sales people with different tax authorities and different areas for sales analysis purposes.
  • Unlimited free form notes can be maintained for each customer and an unlimited number of contacts can be stored against each customer>
  • Email of customer statements to multiple customer contacts
⬆ Top

Entering New Customers

From the menu Receivables tab, click on "Add A New Customer". The customer record is the actual charge account, any number of branches can be defined for each customer account. At least one branch must be defined for each customer. It is the branch details that record the local information about delivery address, tax authority, sales area and sales person.

Customer Code

This field is used as a unique identifier for the customer which is small (maximum of 10 characters of text - letters or numbers). This allows faster searches for customers and keeps the size of the database at a minimum.

Note: A customer code can be altered retrospectively but because of the large scale of the changes required to the system to update stock movement transactions, sales analysis records and sales orders it could present a significant drain on resources. The option to change a customer code is in the utility menu Z_index.php - which must be entered as a manual URL and is only accessible by the system administrator. Such changes should only be undertaken when there are no other users on the system.

Customer Name

The name of the customer is used extensively in lookups and appears on invoices and statements exactly as typed (searches are independent of case). Proper capitalisation and use of the full name of the customer is recommended. The maximum length of the name is 40 characters.

Address Line 1, 2, 3 and 4

This is the address of where invoices and statements are to be posted. A post office box should be entered if applicable. These fields will allow a maximum of 40 characters and are optional. If left out invoices will not show the customer's address which is a requirement for a valid GST or VAT invoice in some administrations.

Currency

This is a compulsory field that identifies the currency in which the customer is to be invoiced. All invoices created for the customer will use this currency and the rate will be used as set up in the currency master - accessible from the General Ledger module. The currency rates need to be maintained at least monthly.

Note: that the rate is recorded in the transaction not the currency. If a customer changes the currency in which they are invoiced it is possible to allocate a new currency receipt against invoices (invoiced in the old currency) in which case the system will calculate large differences on exchange. Note: There is no error check on this and care should be taken, should this occur, to ensure invoices are matched off in the currency in which they were originally created - the cross rate between the new and old currency will provide an equivalent amount of the old currency for entry and allocation.

Invoice Discount

Customers can be set up with a general level of discount which applies to all sales. The percentage entered is used by default on all invoices to the customer. The discount rate can be manually overridden at the time of invoicing, which the system will use to calculate discount. The discount percentage used at invoice time will not be stored as the future default unless the customer details are amended. This field checks to ensure that the percentage is less than 100% and greater or equal to zero. This feature is not currently used/implemented.

Prompt Payment Discount

Customers can be set up with individual prompt payment discount percentages. This field is for memorandum purposes only and shows on screen when customer receipts are entered. If the receipt is on time the discount can be calculated and input with the receipt.

Customer Since

The default is the current date. This field is only used on certain reports where it can be used to restrict the customers shown, and also for credit reference inquiries. The system will only accept a date in this field. The date can be altered at any time. There is no error checking on this field.

Payment Terms

A select box is provided showing the predefined payment terms. New ones can be created as necessary from the Setup tab of the menu. The terms are used to determine whether an account is overdue or not and a description of the terms prints out on invoices, and statements.

There are no restrictions on altering payment terms for a customer at any time. The next statement or invoice produced will show the new terms. The system will only look at the new terms in deciding whether or not invoices are overdue, no record of the terms is held in the transaction itself.

Credit Status or Rating

A lookup is available for this field and a button is available for creation of new credit status categories. Credit status's can be defined to stop any new invoices or indeed orders to the customer - irrespective of his/her credit limit.

A customers Credit Status can be altered at any time.

Note: This will never show on any reports invoices, credits or statement intended for the customers eyes.

Credit Limit

This is a required field which accepts any positive value. It is currently only for memorandum purposes.

Invoice Addressing

This field is a flag that has two choices:

  • To address invoices to the head office postal address. This is the postal address from the customer record as entered above. This is the default option.
  • To address invoices to the branch postal address. This addresses invoices charged to the customer to the branch of the customer, some customers may wish for the branch to authorise invoices before sending on to head office for payment. The branch postal address entered will be used for printing invoices.
⬆ Top

Entering Customer Branches

A customer code entered on its own is insufficient to enter sales orders against. All customers must have at least one branch. The branch records contain the information about the delivery address, the sales area, the tax code, the sales representative and other regional information. New branches can be set up at any time. The first step will always be to select the customer, then to Add/Edit/Delete Customer Branch Records from the Customer menu. There is no limit to the number of branches that can be referenced against a single charge account (customer record). However, branches cannot be transferred between different customers. Only one statement will print per customer, but each invoice will be referenced to the branch it was delivered to.

Branch Name

The branch name can be up to 40 characters long. The branch name is used on packing slips to identify the name to where delivery should be made. It is also used in lookups in sales order entry as it is to the branch that the sale is ordered against. By selecting the branch from this lookup, the customer code and branch code is returned to the system for storing against the order.

Branch Code

The branch code is stored in transactions. It can be up to 10 characters long and should uniquely identify the branch. Two branches cannot have the same code for the same customer. Branch codes (and other codes) cannot contain spaces, commas, & or - . There are checks in place to ensure no new codes are created containing these characters. However, if data is imported it is important to change any codes which contravene these rules.

Branch codes are not available for modification retrospectively. They exist in many tables throughout the database - sales analysis, orders, DebtorTrans and CustTrans and all data in these tables would need to be modified.

Branch Contact / Phone / Fax / Address

The branch contact is the name of the purchasing manager to whom goods and inquiries would be addressed at the branch. A head office branch could be created to identify contact names for account inquiries. It doesn't matter that such a branch may not be invoiced to.

The address is the physical address of the branch for deliveries. As much detail as is required on labels to get the goods to the desired destination should be entered.

Sales Person

A select box is available to enter the salesperson who services this branch.

Draw Stock From

Branches local to a particular warehouse can be associated with the local warehouse by setting this field to the preferred stocking location (see Inventory Locations Maintenance). This affects the entry of sales orders that default to the stock location entered here. It can be overridden at the time of order entry.

Forward Date From A Day In The Month

This field is not currently used.

Delivery Days

This field is not currently used.

Phone/Fax/Email

These are the contact details applicable to the branch.

Tax Authority

The tax authority of the branch determines the regime for tax calculations at invoice and credit time.

Tax Authorities are the authority that collects the taxes. Different authorities in different countries mainly or different states in the USA. Say sales tax in New York is 10% and sales to customers in Michigan attract sales tax at a different rate payable to a different state tax authority.

In the UK, Australia and NZ, the Inland Revenue, Australian Tax Office and the IRD are the relevant tax authorities. Sales to customers that fall under the ATO from a company in NZ do not attract any tax - ie exempt export. However, the same customer who has a branch in Auckland NZ will fall under a different tax authority the NZ IRD - attracting GST @ 12.5% for the same item delivered there.

So the tax authority is the factor relevant based on where the branch of the customer is who is receiving the supply.

The tax authorities are maintained in a separate table (available from the Setup tab) and the tax rate applicable to invoices and credits and the general ledger posting of tax is determined from the Tax Authority setting of the branch together with the applicable level of tax specified in the item (stock) master.

A select box allows the appropriate tax authority for the branch to be selected.

Disable Transactions

This flag - either enabled or disabled - either includes the branch as available for new sales orders or not. If it is set to disabled then the branch will not appear on the order entry branch lookup.

Default Freight Company

A select box allows the selection of the freight company that is most cost/service effective for deliveries to this branch. The entry in this field serves as the default for future sales orders. If it is changed at order entry stage, the overridden entry become the new entry for this field.

Postal Address 1, 2, 3 and 4

This is the postal address of the branch. There is no checking done to ensure this is entered. The only place this would be used is if the customer record required that invoices and credits be addressed to the branch.

⬆ Top

Amending Customer Details

The customer details can be modified at any time and any modifications made will be effective for all future transactions. First select the customer from the link provided on all pages, then select the link for Modify Customer Details.

Points to note:

  • Customer codes can be modified retrospectively using the facility in the utilities menu Z_index.php - this should be used only when all other users are off the system.
  • Changing the payment terms impacts immediately on the aged analysis since this is recalculated each time it is run or a statement is produced.
  • Changing the currency of the customer needs care since the exchange rate is recorded against each transaction. Allocations of one currency against another at different rates will produce differences on exchange. The system will not be able to distinguish at the transactions level which was in what currency only the rate against the functional currency.

Customer Statements

Customer statements can either be printed or emailed directly to all the customers in the selected range, that have a contact defined as receiving a statement. If there are no contacts defined for the customer that have the statement flag set to yes then their statement will not be emailed to them. If the customer has many contacts with several of them having the statement flag set to yes then all those contacts will receive a copy of the pdf statement.

If the customer has any contacts that have the statement flag set then it will not be possible to print their statement so as to avoid sending both a printed statement and an email statement

⬆ Top

Customer Notes

Customer notes containing any text - a web-link if required and a date can be entered from the Select Customer screen - for the selected customer. The notes are displayed in sequence of priority - so pressing issues appear at the top of the list. These notes might contain information about recent contact with the customer or disputes. There is no checking on the content of the notes and no limit to either the number of notes nor the number of characters that can be used.

Customer Type Notes

As well as unlimited notes on individual customers, webERP has the functionality to store an unlimited number of notes on groups of customers based on the debtor type field. As with the notes on individual customers , these notes are displayed in order of priority, and can contain a URL as well as the free form note.

Shippers

This table is only used as a reference to the method of transportation that the invoice delivery was effected by. The shippers name is what is used in the look ups and the code is a system maintained counter which is stored in the database to reference the freight company used. The consignment note reference can be stored against the transaction in the reference field. In this way a full proof of delivery trail can be maintained.

Shipment cost calculations can be automated and the result automatically added to invoices. The least cost shipper is calculated and modified on the order. This system requires active maintenance of the shipment costs tables for each shipper. The shipper costs table shows the cost per kg and metre cubed for freight to destination cities. A substantial amount of data is required. For the system to calculate freight, it also requires that each part have a defined volume and weight set up from which the total order weight and volume is determined for use in the freight calculations.

If freight cost calculations are to be performed at order entry stage, the data must be entered and the options in config.php enabled - see the config.php section.

As with the notes on individual customers , these notes are displayed in order of priority, and can contain a URL as well as the free form note.

Credit Control

Credit control is done by the credit controller, the deputy and the Finance Director. They need the security token Credit control (21). The approval of large write-offs needs the token approval of large bad debt write-offs (22), given to the Finance Director. Sales reps and sales office staff can see credit information, but cannot change a credit status or a credit limit.

Settings

Finance sets the rules in Accounts Receivable, Maintenance, Credit Control Settings: the standard review period in months, whether orders over the credit limit are held, the days between reminder letters, whether the final letter puts the customer on stop, the interest rate, the late fee, the days overdue before charges are made, the general ledger accounts for interest, fees and bad debts, the write-off amount above which the Finance Director must approve, and whether a write-off puts the customer on stop.

Credit reviews, stop and watch

From the Select Customer screen choose Credit Status, Reviews and Reminders. Credit control can:

  • Record a review - the outcome (limit confirmed, raised, reduced, put on watch, put on stop), the new limit, the notes and the next review date. A new limit applies at once, in the same step as the review that explains it. Reviews are kept for ever and cannot be changed or deleted.
  • Change the credit status with a reason. Who, when and why are kept in the credit control history.
  • Exempt the customer from interest and/or late fees, with a reason.
  • Mark invoices as disputed. A disputed invoice is not chased and does not attract interest until the dispute is settled.
  • Add a note, for example that the debt has been passed to a collection agency or to lawyers.

New customers get a next review date automatically, one standard review period after the account is opened. Existing customers were given a date when the system was upgraded.

A customer on stop cannot be given a new order by any route - the sales office, the web shop, EDI or the recurring orders - and goods are not dispatched or invoiced on orders taken before the stop, unless credit control releases the order in Credit Held and Watched Orders. A customer on watch can still be supplied. Whoever takes the order is warned and the orders show on the credit control list. The status is shown wherever staff look at the customer. A customer sees only that the account is on hold, never the watch status.

When an order takes a customer over their credit limit the order is accepted but held. It cannot be dispatched or invoiced until credit control releases it in Credit Held and Watched Orders.

The overdue reminder run

The wording and timing of the letters are kept in Reminder Letter Stages: the number of stages, the days overdue for each and the subject and wording. The wording may use {name}, {debtorno}, {currency}, {amount}, {invoices}, {company} and {date}. Three stages are supplied: a polite reminder, a firmer letter and a final notice.

Credit control starts the run, normally once a week, from Overdue Reminder Run. The run lists who would get which letter. Untick the customers to leave out, for example where a payment is promised, then send. Letters are emailed to the contacts of the customer that receive statements and are recorded against the customer. Customers with no email address are listed so that the letter can be posted. A customer moves up one stage at a time and only while an undisputed invoice is still overdue by the days of the next stage. A customer who pays between the list and the send gets nothing, and a customer is not sent the same stage twice, nor two letters within the minimum days set in the settings. Customers see their reminder letters in the portal.

Month-end interest and late fees

After a month ends, Month-End Interest and Fees lists what would be charged to whom. Interest is a simple annual rate on undisputed invoices overdue by at least the days set in the settings at the end of the month. The late fee is a fixed amount in the home currency, converted to the currency of the customer, charged once per customer per month. Interest and fees are not charged on interest and fees, and exempt customers are not charged. Confirming the list posts a separate, clearly described interest item and fee item to each customer account and to the general ledger income accounts chosen by Finance. They show on the next statement and in the portal. The same month cannot be charged twice. A charge can be waived, with a reason, if it has not been paid. The waiver is also posted to the ledger.

Bad debt write-off

From Bad Debt Write-off credit control writes off all or part of an unpaid balance with a reason. A write-off up to the approval limit is posted at once. A larger one waits for the Finance Director to approve it and does nothing to the account until then. A posted write-off credits the customer account, is allocated to the oldest unpaid invoices and is debited to the bad debt account, with any exchange difference posted as for an allocation. Unless credit control decides otherwise the customer is put on stop. The Bad Debt Write-off Report shows the write-offs over a period with who requested and who approved each one. If a written-off debt is later paid, enter the receipt as an unallocated receipt and use the bad debt recovery process agreed with the Financial Accountant.

Reports

  • Credit Control Report - customers due or overdue for a credit review, customers over their credit limit and by how much, and customers on watch or on stop. It can be filtered by sales rep and by currency and totals are in the home currency. A sales rep sees only their own customers.
  • Aged Customer Balances now also shows each customer's credit limit, credit status and the stage of the last reminder sent.
  • Debtors Ledger Reconciliation - the total of the customer balances against the trade debtors control account, and what explains a difference.

For sales staff

Watch means that you may take orders for the customer but you will be warned and credit control will see the order. Stop means that no order can be entered or invoiced for the customer. Tell the customer to contact credit control and do not try to get around it - the order will not be accepted. Over-limit orders are held until credit control releases them. You can see the status and the reason for it, but you cannot change a status or a limit.

A customer on stop cannot be given a new order by any route - the sales office, the web shop, EDI or the recurring orders - and goods are not dispatched or invoiced on orders taken before the stop, unless credit control releases the order in Credit Held and Watched Orders. A customer on watch can still be supplied. Whoever takes the order is warned and the orders show on the credit control list. The status is shown wherever staff look at the customer. A customer sees only that the account is on hold, never the watch status.

When an order takes a customer over their credit limit the order is accepted but held. It cannot be dispatched or invoiced until credit control releases it in Credit Held and Watched Orders.

The overdue reminder run

The wording and timing of the letters are kept in Reminder Letter Stages: the number of stages, the days overdue for each and the subject and wording. The wording may use {name}, {debtorno}, {currency}, {amount}, {invoices}, {company} and {date}. Three stages are supplied: a polite reminder, a firmer letter and a final notice.

Credit control starts the run, normally once a week, from Overdue Reminder Run. The run lists who would get which letter. Untick the customers to leave out, for example where a payment is promised, then send. Letters are emailed to the contacts of the customer that receive statements and are recorded against the customer. Customers with no email address are listed so that the letter can be posted. A customer moves up one stage at a time and only while an undisputed invoice is still overdue by the days of the next stage. A customer who pays between the list and the send gets nothing, and a customer is not sent the same stage twice, nor two letters within the minimum days set in the settings. Customers see their reminder letters in the portal.

Month-end interest and late fees

After a month ends, Month-End Interest and Fees lists what would be charged to whom. Interest is a simple annual rate on undisputed invoices overdue by at least the days set in the settings at the end of the month. The late fee is a fixed amount in the home currency, converted to the currency of the customer, charged once per customer per month. Interest and fees are not charged on interest and fees, and exempt customers are not charged. Confirming the list posts a separate, clearly described interest item and fee item to each customer account and to the general ledger income accounts chosen by Finance. They show on the next statement and in the portal. The same month cannot be charged twice. A charge can be waived, with a reason, if it has not been paid. The waiver is also posted to the ledger.

Bad debt write-off

From Bad Debt Write-off credit control writes off all or part of an unpaid balance with a reason. A write-off up to the approval limit is posted at once. A larger one waits for the Finance Director to approve it and does nothing to the account until then. A posted write-off credits the customer account, is allocated to the oldest unpaid invoices and is debited to the bad debt account, with any exchange difference posted as for an allocation. Unless credit control decides otherwise the customer is put on stop. The Bad Debt Write-off Report shows the write-offs over a period with who requested and who approved each one. If a written-off debt is later paid, enter the receipt as an unallocated receipt and use the bad debt recovery process agreed with the Financial Accountant.

Reports

  • Credit Control Report - customers due or overdue for a credit review, customers over their credit limit and by how much, and customers on watch or on stop. It can be filtered by sales rep and by currency and totals are in the home currency. A sales rep sees only their own customers.
  • Aged Customer Balances now also shows each customer's credit limit, credit status and the stage of the last reminder sent.
  • Debtors Ledger Reconciliation - the total of the customer balances against the trade debtors control account, and what explains a difference.

For sales staff

Watch means that you may take orders for the customer but you will be warned and credit control will see the order. Stop means that no order can be entered or invoiced for the customer. Tell the customer to contact credit control and do not try to get around it - the order will not be accepted. Over-limit orders are held until credit control releases them. You can see the status and the reason for it, but you cannot change a status or a limit.
